title: Voyager - embeddings + rerank discovery
summary: Discovery on embeddings + reranking. Voyager is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for vector search + rerank. Primary concerns: throughput (200+ qps), hybrid search (BM25 + vector), embedding dimensionality (1536 vs 768), vector DB integration, latency SLOs, security (SSO, KMS, SOC2), and cost. Agreed next step: run a pilot benchmark with topK=100 rerank flow using 50k doc index. Redwood to share benchmark template, security pack, and pricing; schedule technical deep-dive next week.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment
next_steps: Mark to send benchmark template and sample pricing by 2027-05-24
Priya to schedule a technical deep-dive / benchmark run for 2027-05-26
Voyager to share sample dataset (50k docs) and current embedding exports by 2027-05-23
action_items: Priya - schedule and own benchmark run (due 2027-05-26)
Evan - provide dataset export and query workload (due 2027-05-23)
Tom - confirm networking constraints & VPC peering requirements (due 2027-05-25)
transcript:
[00:00] Mark Johnson: hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Mark from Redwood, with Priya our SE. quick intro?
[00:07] Evan Lee: yeah Evan here, CTO at Voyager. we run a search product for enterprise docs, currently using elastic + some FAISS experiments.
[00:14] Priya Patel: awesome, thanks Evan. Sara, Tom, Lina?
[00:18] Sara Gomez: Sara - ML eng, i'm owning embeddings and rerank POC.
[00:21] Tom Wu: Tom - infra/SRE.
[00:23] Lina Park: Lina - product, i'll be watching SLOs and cost.
[00:28] Mark Johnson: great. objective for today is to understand current stack, traffic, what success looks like, and the constraints so we can suggest hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[00:35] Evan Lee: yeah we want to do vector search + rerank. typical query volume is ~120 qps peak but we expect to double during spikes. latency targets are 100-150ms p95 for initial search, rerank can be slightly higher but total tail should be <300ms.
[00:52] Priya Patel: okay, what do you currently use for embeddings and vector db?
[00:56] Sara Gomez: we're generating 1536-d embeddings from a third-party model, storing vectors in an in-house FAISS cluster behind elastic for metadata. we also do a hybrid approach: BM25 first pass then vector re-rank topK=100.
[01:10] Mark Johnson: good pattern. curious — what's the average document size and index size?
[01:14] Sara Gomez: avg doc ~1KB, currently ~50k documents for the pilot, full prod would be ~5M.
[01:20] Tom Wu: infra wise, FAISS is on CPU nodes but we see strain at higher qps; we offload some batched queries overnight.
[01:27] Priya Patel: that helps. for 200 qps with topK=100 rerank, you need to think about batching, kv cache, and whether embeddings are served from dedicated GPUs or precomputed. are your embeddings precomputed?
[01:40] Sara Gomez: yes precomputed. but we sometimes re-embed when models change, which is slow.
[01:44] Mark Johnson: hosted vs dedicated vs private — quick primer: hosted is fastest to get started and we handle infra, dedicated gives reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and lower latency, private moves control plane into your VPC or on-prem for compliance. given you have SRE constraints and expected 5M docs in prod, dedicated or private typically makes sense.
[02:05] Evan Lee: what's the difference in latency/cost if we go hosted vs dedicated?
[02:10] Priya Patel: latency-wise dedicated reduces variability and can hit your 100-150ms p95 better because of reserved GPU capacity and optimized kernels. cost depends on commit, but for steady high-throughput workloads dedicated amortizes better. hosted is pay-as-you-go so it's higher per-token but lower operational overhead.
[02:26] Sara Gomez: how do you integrate with vector DBs? we run FAISS but might move to Milvus or Pinecone.
[02:33] Diego Ramos: we support multiple integration patterns: you can store vectors in your DB and call Redwood for rerank embeddings + scoring (we send vectors or IDs, depending on flow), or we can host vectors in Redwood-managed stores for caching and low-latency rerank. common pattern — BM25 in Elastic first-pass, then pass topK IDs to Redwood to fetch vectors and do efficient neural re-ranking.
[02:51] Tom Wu: if we keep vectors in our VPC, how does networking work?
[02:55] Priya Patel: for Dedicated we do VPC peering or private link; for Private deployment everything runs in your network so no cross-tenant traffic. Hosted can use secure egress to your DB with IP allowlists and TLS. we also support bringing your own KMS for encryption-in-transit and at-rest.
[03:12] Evan Lee: we need SOC2 + SSO via Okta, and audit logs for compliance.
[03:16] Mark Johnson: yes Redwood is SOC2 and we have SAML/Okta and per-token audit logging; we'll share the security pack.
[03:22] Sara Gomez: back to model dims — we're using 1536 dims. we've heard 768 dims reduces cost significantly but maybe loses quality. what's Redwood's guidance?
[03:31] Priya Patel: it's workload dependent. fewer dims often mean faster similarity computation and smaller storage. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization and dimension reduction experiments. for hybrid search, quality often held up better if you keep BM25 strong in the first pass. we also recommend running A/B evals with your rerank gold-set to measure recall/ndcg impact.
[03:52] Lina Park: curious about caching — for rerank can you cache top-k embedding lookups? we'd like to avoid re-fetching vector blobs each request.
[03:59] Diego Ramos: yes, we do prefix and KV caching, and for rerank flows we can cache frequently requested doc vectors in-memory on the serving tier to cut fetch latency. cache invalidation is hookable to your indexing pipeline.
[04:12] Tom Wu: what about quantization and accuracy tradeoffs? we can't have big regressions on legal docs.
[04:17] Priya Patel: we support 8-bit and mixed quant profiles; Redwood Optimize can recommend profiles by workload. for legal docs we recommend conservative quantization and run regression checks; we tie quality monitoring to your eval sets.
[04:29] Evan Lee: what sort of throughput can dedicated handle for rerank? like topK=100, 200 qps.
[04:35] Priya Patel: depends on GPU type and model. with A100-class in reserved pools and batching, we can hit 200 qps for an efficient dot-product rerank pipeline with ~150ms latency, but you need proper batching, kernel tuning, and sometimes sharding. we can run a benchmark with your data to validate.
[04:54] Sara Gomez: internal concern: embedding store consistency when we reindex — re-embedding at scale will take hours. can Redwood help with incremental re-embeddings?
[05:03] Diego Ramos: we have reindexing helpers and incremental rollout patterns; you can version embeddings and run canary rollouts so search isn't impacted.
[05:10] Mark Johnson: let's talk cost- roughly if you do hosted with our standard 1536-d model it's pay-per-request; dedicated comes with monthly commit and lower per-token. we'll send sample pricing.
[05:21] Lina Park: we also have data residency: EU-only for some clients. can Redwood host in EU region?
[05:26] Priya Patel: yes, we have regions and can pin workloads to EU. Private deployment is best for full on-prem/residency requirements.
[05:33] Evan Lee: any references or benchmarks with hybrid BM25 + vector rerank we could review?
[05:37] Mark Johnson: yes we'll send a benchmark spreadsheet and a sample evaluation repo. Priya will run an initial benchmark using your 50k dataset with topK=100 and measure p95 latency and ndcg against your gold queries.
[05:49] Tom Wu: security docs please, and network diagrams for dedicated/private.
[05:52] Mark Johnson: will do.
[05:54] Sara Gomez: question — for the rerank step, is it better to send raw embeddings from our DB or send IDs and let Redwood fetch vectors?
[06:01] Priya Patel: sending IDs is common when vectors live in your DB; Redwood will fetch and do the ranking in the serving runtime. sending embeddings avoids the extra fetch but increases payload size; tradeoffs depend on network and serialization overhead. if vectors are large and you have high qps, keeping vectors in a co-located store or using dedicated infra reduces latency.
[06:21] Evan Lee: ok what would the pilot look like?
[06:24] Mark Johnson: we propose: 1) Voyager shares 50k sample + gold queries 2) Redwood runs hosted benchmark (or dedicated if you prefer) with topK=100 rerank, measure latency/ndcg/cost 3) review results and propose Dedicated sizing or Private plan.
[06:38] Lina Park: timeline? we want results within two weeks.
[06:41] Priya Patel: that's feasible. we'll schedule the benchmark next week and aim to deliver results within 7-10 days after dataset handoff.
[06:49] Mark Johnson: recap and next steps — we'll send security pack, benchmark template, pricing, and schedule deep-dive.
[06:56] Evan Lee: great, thanks everyone.
[07:00] Mark Johnson: thanks, end.
